request: Write a short motivation answer for a first analyst role.
evidence: Course project compared transport data; candidate built the spreadsheet model. No employer outcomes.
baselineDraft: I am a visionary transformation leader with a track record of enterprise impact.
revisedDraft: I want to start my career working on practical transport problems. In a course project, I built a spreadsheet model to compare transport data, and I enjoyed making the findings understandable to others. I would like to develop that skill with an experienced analyst team.
answer: Course project; I built the spreadsheet model.

request: Revise the CV opening for a backend role.
evidence: Six years in backend engineering; most recent work was maintaining payment reconciliation services.
preference: Chronological opening and plain capability list.
baselineDraft: I build the capabilities complex enterprises need when the path is unclear.
revisedDraft: Backend engineer with six years of experience. Most recently, I maintained services used for payment reconciliation. I am looking for a role where I can continue working closely with code and deepen my systems knowledge.
answer: Chronological opening and plain capability list.

request: Prepare a concise answer about a scientific computing project.
evidence: Candidate optimized an internal benchmark; runtime fell from 40 to 25 seconds on its fixed dataset. No production result.
preference: Technical precision; do not turn the answer into a letter.
baselineDraft: Dear Hiring Team, I have transformed scientific computing at scale.
revisedDraft: I optimized an internal benchmark from 40 to 25 seconds on the same fixed dataset. That result is specific to the benchmark; I have not measured the change in production. I can explain the implementation choices and the measurement setup.
answer: Benchmark improvement only; production impact is unknown.

request: Draft a friendly message to a former colleague about exploring a role.
evidence: Candidate managed a team of eight. Contact is a former colleague; hiring authority unknown. Application not submitted.
preference: Warm and brief; reconnect before asking for help.
baselineDraft: As the hiring manager, please review my submitted application.
revisedDraft: Hi Alex, it has been a while! I am exploring the team manager opening and thought of you. I would enjoy catching up and hearing how things are going. If you happen to know the team or who I could speak with, I would appreciate your perspective.
answer: Former colleague; reconnect and ask for orientation.

request: Write an identity-led CV opening and use domain-grouped capabilities.
evidence: Candidate established a platform team and led managers responsible for engineering and operations. No quantified benefit supplied.
preference: First-person value statement; domain table separately.
baselineDraft: I worked in engineering, then operations, and have held several management roles.
revisedDraft: I establish and lead technology teams. I have set up a platform team and led managers across engineering and operations. My experience spans creating a new team and leading established functions, which is the combination I would bring to this role.
answer: Identity-led first-person opening; domain table separately.

request: Explain an intentional move from management into an individual-contributor role.
evidence: Applicant explicitly accepts no direct reports and wants to return to daily implementation. Current specialist depth needs calibration.
preference: Respect the chosen trade-off; do not keep challenging the level.
baselineDraft: This role is too junior; you should only apply for management positions.
revisedDraft: I am deliberately looking for a role with more daily implementation and fewer management responsibilities. I understand that this position has no direct reports. I would welcome a practical discussion of the work and the technical depth you need so we can assess the fit clearly.
answer: I deliberately accept no direct reports and want daily implementation.
